verdict.rationale: Pylon documents a first-party API to 'programmatically access and take action on data' and publishes a 119-path OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec, so broad programmatic coverage exists. Nothing documents that the API matches the UI feature-for-feature, and the changelog shows endpoints like GET /task-statuses only now being added, which suggests parity is incomplete. The MCP server is limited to reading and updating issues, accounts, and contacts. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, evidence of API coverage for configuration surfaces (triggers, agents, dashboards, knowledge base, field and settings management), and independent or hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Pylon's API can be used to programmatically access and take action on data within Pylon.
Pylon publishes a complete OpenAPI 3.0.3 document at its API origin (info title "Pylon API.", 119 paths, US and EU server entries)
Added a GET /task-statuses API endpoint for enumerating configured task statuses
AI tools authenticate with your Pylon account via OAuth and can read and update issues, accounts, and contacts within the data you can see in Pylon.
